item.title: Book review: How Not to Be Wrong. The Power of Mathematical Thinking
item.description:
Why this Book?

Mathematics is something that either brings back bad memories or something you might enjoyed early on but failed to see it’s relevance in real life. “How Not to Be Wrong” chooses to challenge this perception, revealing mathematics as a vibrant, practical tool for understanding the world around us.

Jordan Ellenberg explains problems where math isn’t confined to classrooms or academic papers, it’s woven into the fabric of everyday life, from the lottery tickets we buy to the medical studies we read about, from political polls to questions about the existence of God.

item.title: Book review: A Gentleman in Moscow
item.description:
Why this Book?

I don’t review books often, but sometimes a book is so good it deserves praise worthy of the attention, detail, and uniqueness the author managed to bring to life.

A Gentleman in Moscow is one such book. It made me gain a wider appreciation for the old-school manners, charms, and etiquette of aristocratic societies.

Background

Count Alexandar Rostov was born into nobility and over the years, spent time paying attention to what most folks would call banal.
